claims.text: The initial FeCoNiCrMn alloy is an as-cast, homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Interstitial nitrogen can be incorporated into FeCoNiCrMn by melting under nitrogen or by plasma nitriding at approximately 400–500°C for several hours.
Several hours of reactive processing at 400–500°C can provide sufficiently uniform nitrogen diffusion.
Controlled nitrogen incorporation will cause in situ formation of fine nitride precipitates in FeCoNiCrMn.
The nitrogen-induced precipitates will include Fe- or Co-nitride phases.
The nitride precipitates will be finely and uniformly dispersed in the alloy matrix under the proposed processing conditions.
Fine nitride precipitates act as pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Pinning by nitride precipitates impedes magnetic domain-wall motion.
Increased resistance to domain-wall displacement raises the coercive field relative to an otherwise matched nitrogen-free alloy.
Nitrogen-treated FeCoNiCrMn will have a coercive field approximately 20–40% higher than the nitrogen-free baseline.
Coarse or unevenly distributed precipitates may diminish or eliminate the coercivity increase.
Significant nitrogen-induced changes in grain size may diminish or eliminate the coercivity increase.
A coercive-field increase below 10%, or one that is not statistically significant, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted increase is 20–40%, but the falsification rule only rejects increases below 10%; an observed 10–19% increase would fall outside the prediction without falsifying it.

The boundary treats coarse or clustered precipitates as processing deviations under which the effect may not hold, whereas the falsification rule treats observing such precipitates as sufficient to falsify the hypothesis.
